translations.translatedText: # Sunday 15.9.2019 (radio)
Environmental crimes seldom go to court. Traffic signs are being renewed next summer. Lots of rain is now needed to fill groundwater stores.
## Environmental crimes are not easy to solve
![Mustapuro stream in East Helsinki.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10328556)
Open image viewer
A strange chemical was floating in the Mustapuro stream in East Helsinki a little over a year ago. J Photo: Olli-Pekka Kursi / Yle
Most environmental crimes never go as far as court.
Around 450 suspected environmental crimes come to the police's preliminary investigation every year. Of these, 75 percent do not go on to court.

Leila Suvantola, a researcher at the University of Eastern Finland, says that many suspected environmental crimes do not go to court, because the police cannot find out who committed the crime. Many crimes also become time-barred, so their investigation is stopped.
The Helsinki police receive about 50 suspected environmental crimes a year. A typical case is that waste has been dumped into a stream or ditch, or that waste has been released straight into a drain.
## Traffic signs are renewed
![a traffic sign in the picture.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9889370)
Open image viewer
A new pedestrian crossing sign. Photo: Yle
The appearance of many traffic signs is changing.
![Traffic sign warning of deer](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10828937)
Open image viewer
A traffic sign warning of deer
The new Road Traffic Act comes into force next June. Because of this, a few new traffic signs will be introduced, and at the same time many old traffic signs will be renewed a little.

For example, the pedestrian crossing sign is being renewed. On the old sign, a figure walking across the crossing looks like a man. On the new sign, the figure on the crossing has a gender or age that cannot be known.
The new traffic signs include, for example, a sign that warns of deer, and a sign that bans the use of studded tyres on a certain stretch of road.
However, all traffic signs are still such that, even after the renewal, you understand what a sign means at one glance.
## Groundwater is low

![Water is leaving the shores of Lake Hirvijärvi. The level of the lake has never been this low during its measurement history.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10521245)
Open image viewer
The surfaces of many lakes are also lower than usual. Photo: Antti Kettumäki/Yle
Many wells have now run dry. The wells have dried up, because the groundwater has dropped very low.
The driest areas are in Central Finland, North Savo and the southern part of Kainuu.
In July and August, very little rain fell. Only once in 30 years has there been a summer this dry.
The surfaces of many lakes are also lower than usual for this time of year.

Bertel Vehviläinen, a hydrologist at the Finnish Environment Institute, says that a lot of rain is needed now. Rain is needed so that the groundwater stores fill before winter comes. If not enough rain comes, or if winter starts early, the wells will be dry until spring, Bertel Vehviläinen says.
